bpa.hero.h1: Besides piles, which other diseases affect the anal passage?
bpa.hero.lede: Not every anal problem is piles — which conditions occur here, and where a correct diagnosis is made, in plain language.
bpa.fig.cap: Image from the clinic's education post — anorectal diseases
bpa.intro.p2: The mistake we commonly make is to assume that any problem in the anal passage is piles. That is why we should know which other diseases besides piles occur in the anal passage.
bpa.intro.p3: Those diseases are… 1. Piles/Haemorrhoid 2. Anal Fissure
bpa.h2.list: Diseases that can occur in the anal passage
bpa.h2.list.lede: Below is a one-glance, general idea of the main diseases that can occur in the anal passage — not for diagnosing yourself by reading it.
bpa.c1.p: Piles develop when the veins at the lowest part of the rectum and around the anus swell under pressure. Bright red blood when passing stool, itching or pain around the area, or a soft lump — these are common signs of piles. In many people the symptoms settle with simple care; still, the cause of any bleeding should first be checked by a doctor.
bpa.c2.t: Anal fissure (a tear in the anal lining)
bpa.c2.p: A fissure is a small tear in the thin lining inside the anal canal. Sharp, knife-like or burning pain when passing stool, pain that continues for hours afterwards, and traces of blood on the toilet paper — these are common signs of a fissure. Constipation and hard stools are often the cause.
bpa.c3.p: A fistula is a small tunnel that forms between the inside of the anal canal and the skin near it. Repeated discharge of pus or fluid near the anus, along with irritation and swelling — these are its common signs. A fistula usually does not heal on its own, so the earlier it is examined, the simpler the treatment tends to be.
bpa.c4.p: An abscess forms when pus collects near the anus because of an infection. Pain and swelling that build up quickly, or shivering and fever with feeling very unwell, mean you should see a doctor quickly — in many cases the pain starts to ease once the pus is drained.
bpa.c5.p: A pilonidal sinus is a small hole or tunnel in the skin at the top of the cleft between the buttocks. When hair is pushed under the skin by pressure and friction, that area can get infected again and again; a painful swelling or a pus-filled abscess can make sitting difficult.
bpa.c6.t: Anal skin tag (a small flap of skin)
bpa.c6.p: A small, soft lump of skin around the anus — in most cases harmless, and often left behind after piles settle or a fissure heals. Still, other conditions can look similar, so it is safest to have any new lump identified by a doctor first.
bpa.h2.dx: How is a correct diagnosis made?
bpa.dx.p1: The same symptom can belong to more than one disease — assuming a disease without an examination is risky. A correct diagnosis is made only through a doctor's examination: listening to the problem, the necessary tests, and, where needed, special investigations — these steps bring out the real cause.
bpa.dx.p2: So whether it is blood with stool, pain, a lump or discharge — whatever the symptom is, get examined instead of assuming. Detailed information on the main diseases mentioned here is on our treatment pages:
